summary: Recorded the drift-then-snapshot receipt and moved the snapshot question to violated. After the drift (the three nodes reporting accepted 9, 9 and 6 with decided 9 while the leader held six indices of content), the public snapshot(Some(8), false) returned Ok, advanced the leader's compacted index to 8, and the snapshot the leader now serves for index 0 held zero entry ids — none of the five decided entries the log contained — while the leader's accepted index stayed 6 and its decided index 9; the declared comparisons requiring the compacted index to stay at the six indices of content and the snapshot to hold the five entries were both violated at that event, and the comparison requiring the call to be accepted came out unknown only because its admission chain shared an event name with another case in the same execution while the operand shows Ok. A behaviour records that the snapshot bound and the snapshot range both come from drifted values and that an empty range yields a snapshot with no entries; the interpretation is violated/asserted with the mechanism spelled out (try_snapshot bounds by the decided index, which the documented note permits, while create_snapshot builds from the range starting at the current compacted index and the in-memory storage returns nothing for a non-existent range), keeps the counterevidence explicit (the call returned Ok so nothing in its result signals the loss; the index used was inside the documented allowance; the StopSign equal-case adjustment is not what produced this witness), and lists the limits (dependence on the entry type's snapshot, unanalysed peer-side compaction beyond the sampled indexes, one size/round/index/entry type, and the shared-name admission limitation). The question's discriminator now asks about a request equal to the drifted decided index, a follower-side request, other entry types and the peers' end state. No execution was requested this turn; incomplete are those variants, the trim child's other-producer question, the drift parent's bound and reconfiguration-handoff questions, timers and loss triggers, larger clusters, persistence, and any further independent lead.
